question: Should this behavior-preserving heartbeat refactor be accepted after the branch is refreshed to current `main` and a maintainer verifies real runner output for delivery and finalization ordering?
rationale: The PR carries a protected `maintainer` label and restructures the central heartbeat lifecycle; automated checks support it, but they cannot by themselves establish that the intended ordering remains unchanged in a real run.

options.title: Request runtime proof and refresh
options.body: Rebase onto current `main` and add redacted output from a real heartbeat wake that demonstrates the expected result, delivery, and finalization order.

options.title: Review the staged boundary directly
options.body: A heartbeat-area owner can accept the refactor based on a full current-head lifecycle review if they judge the existing focused test evidence sufficient.

recommendation.title: Request runtime proof and refresh
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current `main` and add redacted output from a real heartbeat wake that demonstrates the expected result, delivery, and finalization order.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and are assigned to the staged runner change, so they are the best available contact to supply the intended invariant and refreshed proof.
